full.answer: Part 82 is a depth, not a physical component. It is the depth that head unit 12 reaches while being lowered, at the point where force sensors 50 and 52 start to read a rapidly rising force as they meet the denser bearing layer BL. On the way down, the sensors read lower force levels until the unit reaches depth 82 (FIG. 3A). The sharp rise in force there can be used to find the depth and/or thickness of the debris layer and the location of the bearing layer. In the sequence, depth 80 comes first (force is still zero until then; FIG. 3), then depth 82, then depth 84, where the forces level off (FIG. 3B). The description discusses this sequence with reference to the FIG. 4 force/displacement graph. On the drawings, 82 is labelled in FIG. 3A on sheet p4 (D4-55) and on the FIG. 4 graph on sheet p6 (D6-2).

text_only.answer: Part 112 is the "match checking step" in the FIG. 5 flow chart, which shows how the network adapter coalesces packets in chunks. At this step the network adapter checks whether the packet it just received matches the packet stored before it, so their payloads can be coalesced. The goal is to find runs of packets whose payloads the driver can combine into one large packet. One test is whether the two packets have consecutive sequence numbers. If they match, the adapter goes to step 114 and sets the completion-queue indication to "match". If they don't, it goes to the gap determination step 152. The completion-queue entry then reports whether a match occurred at step 112. The description places step 112 in FIG. 5. No drawing labels were provided for this patent, so I can't point to a label spot for 112 on any sheet.

Part 16 is the energy storage device. It holds the return energy that drives the part 12 into a set end position if the drive fails. It appears in Figs. 1, 2 and 3, but I couldn't cite any drawing label spots because no OCR label list was provided for the sheets.

What it is: It is mounted on the actuator's outer housing 14 as a separate, externally closed assembly unit. Inside, a gear wheel 62 meshes with two opposing gear racks 64, and each rack has a pair of compression springs (66, 68 or 70, 72) that store the return energy. When the drives fail, the holding devices release and the stored energy is let out all at once.

full.answer:
Part 48 is a pin on the second gear wheel 36. It is one of the stop surfaces of the mechanical rotary entrainment device 40 that links the second output shaft 38 to the first output shaft 34.

- Mounting: pin 48 is fitted into an axial opening in gear wheel 36, alongside a second pin, 46.
- Function: the pins act as stop surfaces that let the two coaxial output shafts be coupled in the direction of rotation.
- Position: pins 46 and 48 sit on the same circle around the shared central axis of output shafts 34 and 38.
- Mating pin: pin 50 on the first gear wheel 32 is on the same circle and comes into contact with pins 46 and 48.
- Loading the energy storage device: when the first drive turns, pin 50 pushes pin 48 anticlockwise. This carries the second output shaft along and tensions the springs.
- Fail-safe return: if the drives fail, the released energy storage device turns gear wheel 36 clockwise. Pin 48 then pushes pin 50, which drives the first output shaft 34 and moves the part to its first end position.

full.answer:
Part 26 is the second high temperature coil. It is a coil in the convection section that heats the feedstock/dilution steam mixture one last time. This happens after the mixture comes out of the primary transfer line exchanger 35 and before it enters the radiant section 10.

What it does:
- After the mixture leaves transfer line exchanger 35, it is heated further by coil 26 in the convection section, before it enters the radiant section.
- Because this coil does the final heating, the transfer line exchanger's cold-side outlet can run cooler, at about 550 °C instead of more than 600 °C. That gives a larger log-mean temperature difference in the exchanger, which improves product yield.
- It is preferably placed in the bottom part of the convection section. The high pressure steam superheater(s) 25 sit downstream of it, so the coil also protects the superheater from overheating.

Part 35 is the primary transfer line exchanger in the cooling section. I can't point to where it appears on the drawings, because no drawing labels were provided with this patent.

What it is: The reference list names 35 as the "Primary transfer line exchanger." In FIG. 1 (cracking furnace system 40), the feedstock/dilution steam mixture 13 is heated in the first high temperature coil 23 and then in the primary transfer line exchanger 35.

What it does: The cracked gas 8 leaving the radiant section is cooled quickly in exchanger 35, which stops the reactions while they still favour the products. The heat taken from the cracked gas warms the feedstock-diluent mixture 13. The mixture then goes back to the convection section to be heated further in the second high temperature coil 26 before it enters radiant section 10. A secondary transfer line exchanger 36 sits downstream of 35 and boils boiler water.
